AN05B023b/c: sensory drive and downstream partners

Setup

Read 08_an05b023bc_cut.Rmd alongside this page. AN05B023b is cut off in the brain, so every difference below that involves a partner beyond that point is a statement about where the reconstruction ended, not about the neurons. 06 runs the same plots with AN05B023c truncated at the plane where AN05B023b stops.

rgl cannot initialise headless on this machine, so rgl.useNULL is set before anything that might pull it in.

Everything that fetches or draws lives in _an_pair.R, shared with 07_an05b023cd.Rmd so the two comparisons cannot drift apart. What stays here is the pair and what is said about it.

options(rgl.useNULL = TRUE)   # must precede any library that pulls rgl in (nat)

suppressMessages({
  library(neuprintr); library(malecns); library(nat)
  options(malecns.dataset = "male-cns:v1.0")   # malecns helpers ignore MCNS_DATASET
  library(coconatfly); library(coconat)
  library(dplyr); library(tibble)
  library(ggplot2); library(ggrepel); library(scales); library(patchwork)
})

R_DIR <- "/Users/fkampf/Documents/pheromone.paper/analyses/an_investigation/R"

# _paths.R falls back to an05b023bc, but AN_CASE may already be set to another
# case from an earlier 01-03 run in this session, so pin it here.
Sys.setenv(AN_CASE = "an05b023bc")
source(file.path(R_DIR, "_paths.R"))
source(file.path(R_DIR, "_an_pair.R"))
neuprint_login(server = MCNS_SERVER, dataset = MCNS_DATASET)

PAIR <- TARGET_TYPES   # left of zero, right of zero
PAIR
## [1] "AN05B023b" "AN05B023c"

Annotation tables are expensive to fetch, so they are cached in the global environment for the session.

load_once <- function(name, expr, envir = .GlobalEnv) {
  # eval() here evaluates a quote()d expression written literally in this file -
  # it is a lazy-evaluation idiom for "only run this fetch if not already cached",
  # not a parser of external input.
  if (!exists(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)) {
    assign(name, eval(expr), envir = envir)
  }
  get(name, envir = envir)
}
# No BANC here: this page is a maleCNS-only follow-up. For a BANC cross-check,
# copy the guarded fct / fba block from 04_SN_AN_connections.Rmd (lines 48-65) -
# reticulate::py_require("caveclient") has to run before python initialises.

mba <- load_once("mba", quote(mcns_body_annotations()))

The sensory pool

Leg and wing gustatory bristle neurons. Wider than the receptor-typed set on purpose: the generic taste bristles act as a built-in negative control, so if the pheromone candidates fail to separate from them that is itself a result.

sensory_pool() drops bodies with no type, both NA and "" — neuprint returns the empty string, which is why load_mba() in pheromone.paper/R/data_processing.R converts it, and these pages fetch from neuprint rather than from mba.feather.

Consequence of that same choice: type here is the bare server name, so the _ADMN / _ProLN suffix variants documented in _paths.R do not appear and bare_type() is a no-op on this table. Read mba.feather instead if the suffix split matters.

contact_pool <- sensory_pool(mba)

length(contact_pool)
## [1] 1067

Downstream output of each type

mcns_connection_table(..., 'o') puts the query body in bodyid and the partner in partner; its type column describes the partner, so grouping on type already gives the postsynaptic type. Dropping partners that are in contact_pool removes the sensory bristles, leaving the genuinely downstream side — and the sensory section below keeps exactly what this one discards.

l_output <- type_edges(paste0("/type:", PAIR[1]), "o", contact_pool)
r_output <- type_edges(paste0("/type:", PAIR[2]), "o", contact_pool)

setNames(c(sum(l_output$total), sum(r_output$total)), PAIR)
## AN05B023b AN05B023c 
##      4842      9494

b vs c: difference

Both types are two bodies (one per side, both GABAergic), so the raw weight totals are directly comparable and no per-cell scaling is needed. The two overall output totals printed above are the caveat to watch: if one type makes substantially more synapses than the other, every bar shifts in its direction, so read frac_diff (each partner’s share of that type’s own downstream output) alongside diff before calling a partner type specific.

diff_of() full-joins the two, so partners seen by only one become 0 on the other side rather than dropping out, which is exactly the case the plot is for.

out_diff <- diff_of(l_output, r_output)

out_diff |> select(type, total_l, total_r, diff, frac_diff)

The bars run bottom to top, most b-biased (negative) to most c-biased (positive). MIN_DIFF only controls readability — with every partner type on one axis the labels are unreadable — so the count of types it hides is printed rather than left implicit.

MIN_DIFF <- 20   # synapses; a type must differ by at least this to get a bar

shown <- out_diff |> filter(abs(diff) >= MIN_DIFF)
sprintf("%d of %d partner types shown; %d hidden below |diff| = %d",
        nrow(shown), nrow(out_diff), nrow(out_diff) - nrow(shown), MIN_DIFF)
## [1] "109 of 720 partner types shown; 611 hidden below |diff| = 20"

A difference says nothing about scale on its own: 300 synapses is the whole story on a partner that receives 800 inputs and a rounding error on one that receives 20,000. The right-hand panel carries that. It is fetched only for the types that survive MIN_DIFF, which is what keeps this from being the slow all-partners call, and it is edge weights again, so it is on the same footing as the bars.

The dimorphism colours are deliberately a different hue family from the blue/pink pair colours: purple for male-specific, teal for sexually dimorphic, pale for the “potentially” calls, grey for unannotated. Nothing about a colour here should read as bias toward b or c.

bars_out <- bars_downstream(shown, mba)

count(bars_out, grp)

The absolute counts go on top of the difference bars as one line per row: its left end is how many synapses AN05B023b gives that partner, its right end how many AN05B023c gives it. Both ends are plotted as positive counts, b mirrored to the left of zero, so the x axis reads outward from the centre in both directions and the tick labels are abs().

The bar and the line are the same two numbers seen two ways: the line’s midpoint sits at half the difference, so a line centred on zero is a partner both neurons drive equally, however long it is.

One consequence of sharing an axis: partners with thousands of synapses stretch the scale and squash the difference bars. That is the honest relationship between the two quantities, but if the bars become unreadable, drop the line onto its own panel instead.

bc_plot(bars_out,
        pair      = PAIR,
        lab_cols  = unname(DIMORPH_COLS[as.character(bars_out$grp)]),
        grp_cols  = DIMORPH_COLS,
        x_lab     = sprintf("bars: %s − %s    dots: synapses given by %s (left) and %s (right)",
                            PAIR[2], PAIR[1], PAIR[1], PAIR[2]),
        share_lab = "share of that type's input from the pair")

Output onto dimorphic partners

Which of the two sends more of its output to partners the dataset calls dimorphic or sex-specific. Computed on out_diff, the whole downstream table rather than the MIN_DIFF subset, because this is a property of each type’s entire output and thresholding first would drop the tail where an annotated class can hide.

frac_l / frac_r are shares of that type’s own total, so “more” here survives one of the two simply being the bigger neuron.

dimorph_out <- dimorph_output(out_diff, mba)

dimorph_out

Total share onto annotated partners, per type:

setNames(colSums(dimorph_out[dimorph_out$dimorphism != "not annotated",
                             c("frac_l", "frac_r")]), PAIR)
## AN05B023b AN05B023c 
## 0.1030566 0.1387192
dimorph_output_plot(dimorph_out, PAIR)

Read the bar lengths first — that is the answer to “which one” — and the segments only for which class carries it. Note that not annotated is the majority class in mba, so both bars are short by construction; the comparison is between them, not against 100%.

Sensory input to b and c

The mirror image of the plot above, on the types that type_edges() excluded there: the leg and wing gustatory bristles of contact_pool. Left end of each line is what that bristle type gives AN05B023b, right end what it gives AN05B023c, and the bar is still c − b.

There is no MIN_DIFF here. The pool holds 27 types, few enough to show whole, and on the input side a type contributing nothing to one of the two is exactly the observation worth keeping visible.

l_input <- type_edges(paste0("/type:", PAIR[1]), "i", contact_pool, sensory = TRUE)
r_input <- type_edges(paste0("/type:", PAIR[2]), "i", contact_pool, sensory = TRUE)

in_diff <- diff_of(l_input, r_input)

in_diff |> select(type, total_l, total_r, diff, frac_diff)

The second panel inverts too. Downstream it asked what share of the partner’s input comes from b and c; here it asks what share of the bristle type’s whole output lands on them — the same question about how much of the relationship the pair actually owns, read from the sensory side. bars_sensory() builds both the denominator and the subclass lookup from pool bodies only; the reason is written out in _an_pair.R, and it matters for SNxxxx, LgLG2 and LgLG4.

No dimorphism colours on this one: every body in the pool is unannotated for dimorphism, so that scale would come out uniformly grey. subclass is what the pool does carry, so the second panel is filled by leg versus wing bristle.

The four FOCUS types are picked out in bold rather than in WEB_PALETTE: that palette gives LgLG1a the same pink and LgLG1b the same blue that already mean c and b in this plot, so using it on the labels would put two meanings on one colour. Types are named as the connectome names them, so no receptor-channel grouping is implied.

bars_in <- bars_sensory(in_diff, mba, contact_pool)

is_focus <- as.character(bars_in$type) %in% FOCUS

bc_plot(bars_in,
        pair      = PAIR,
        lab_cols  = ifelse(is_focus, DARK_FG, DARK_DIM),
        grp_cols  = SUBCLASS_COLS,
        x_lab     = sprintf("bars: %s − %s    dots: synapses onto %s (left) and %s (right)",
                            PAIR[2], PAIR[1], PAIR[1], PAIR[2]),
        share_lab = "share of that bristle type's output onto the pair",
        lab_face  = ifelse(is_focus, "bold", "plain"))
